features.note: The enclosure reads unambiguously as a walled boundary inside the bay — a distinct volume you cannot confuse with loose equipment. The damper pair is the strongest element in the entire capture set: coupling-exhaust-off shows a solid filled dark rectangle (flat closed blades) and coupling-exhaust-full shows an open grille with two fan-hub circles clearly visible behind the open slats — the boundary heat does or does not cross is legible. Two exhaust fans confirmed through the open-louver state. In bay-envelope.png the louver aperture is also visible on the exterior end wall, confirming the enclosure reads from outside the building. Minor: the compressor-room camera preset is partially occluded by the trunk duct filling the upper 40% of frame, reducing legibility of that view.

EXPLICIT Q1 — LUMINAIRE COUNT: From luminaire-grid.png (oblique interior view looking down the bay), approximately 9-10 distinct luminaire bodies with clear body+lit-lens form can be individually resolved. Closer fixtures (roughly the nearest two rows) show the correct UFO highbay form: a dark cylindrical body with a bright white circular disc lens. The 18th count cannot be confirmed from this single oblique angle — distant fixtures collapse to small bright dots and the leftmost column of the 6-wide grid is partly obscured by the duct and the left-wall column line. Grid regularity is implied by even spacing along the longitudinal axis; the 3-row transverse arrangement is readable as two lateral groupings visible in the shot. The coupling-lights-off capture confirms emissive response: the lens glow disappears cleanly at dim=0. Feature scores at threshold, not above it, because the 6x3 plan arrangement cannot be fully confirmed from the current camera angle.

The AHU box on the roof, the metallic riser dropping down, and the trunk duct running the full bay length are all confirmed across ahu-roof.png and duct-run.png. The riser-to-duct junction is the clearest joint in the set — the metallic cylinder seats directly onto the cylindrical duct crown with no gap or float. Green arrow markers on the duct underside indicate diffuser positions; these render as flow-direction icons rather than as physical diffuser cone geometry, but the continuous air path from AHU through riser to trunk duct is unambiguous. No floating duct segments. The trunk duct itself has strong metallic reflectance and reads as a real galvanized spiral duct at blockout.

FAIL. EXPLICIT Q2 — MACHINES OR BOXES: The two compressor packages in compressor-room-open.png read as dark featureless rectangular boxes. They are indistinguishable from storage crates, equipment plinths, or concrete blocks. There is no cooling-fan grille on any face, no horizontal canopy-to-base break line, no control panel plate. One box has a faint circular mark on its front face but it does not resolve as a grille or fan ring at this exposure. The receiver is correctly identifiable — the blue dome-capped cylinder with the correct proportional height is the one element that reads as real industrial hardware. The dryer reads as a small plain box. The header pipe is a single thin faint line, barely legible. The compressor packages themselves are the dominant identity failure: the spec requires 'enclosed canopy with cooling-fan grille' and the current geometry provides neither.

FAIL. Bay proportions are correct: the plan ratio reads approximately 2:1 which is right for 40x20 m, and bay-envelope.png confirms the building reads as a closed industrial structure. Wall cladding is present and gives the correct light-grey metal-panel appearance. However the column grid is expressed only as thin flat vertical seam lines on the cladding faces — no structural profile with any cross-sectional depth or reveal is visible from any capture. In bay-envelope.png (roof ON), the ceiling is a solid flat plane with no truss geometry; the spec requires roof trusses. The building currently reads as a smooth hollow box rather than a steel-frame structure with a defined structural rhythm. Columns and trusses are the missing blockout geometry.

important_features.note: A thin pipe line is faintly visible in duct-run.png running along the right wall at high level, and the header connecting compressor to receiver appears in compressor-room-open.png as a thin wire. Route is plausible and at high level. However the pipe reads as a hairline in both shots — at this scale and darkness it does not register confidently as a distribution main. Present but below the 'sensibly routed' read for an important feature.

The golden-tan humanoid figure is present in duct-run.png (centre floor, mid-bay) and luminaire-grid.png (lower centre). It effectively makes the 8 m clear height legible and gives the trunk duct diameter and compressor enclosure height a human reference. Correct floor placement. No objection at blockout fidelity.

defects.description: Both compressor package meshes are featureless dark boxes with no geometry differentiating them from inert crates. Missing: cooling-fan grille on the canopy top face, horizontal canopy-break seam at mid-height, and a control panel plate on the front face. The current meshes cannot be read as rotary screw compressors from any camera angle.

Column grid is absent as structural geometry — only flat cladding seam lines exist. Roof trusses are absent — bay-envelope.png shows a solid flat ceiling plane. The spec requires both to prevent the bay from reading as a hollow box. The structural rhythm that makes an industrial building legible is missing.

The luminaire-grid camera preset is oblique and low (~20 deg elevation), preventing a count of all 18 fixtures and unambiguous confirmation of the 6x3 plan grid. Only 9-10 bodies can be individually resolved; the rest collapse to dots or are occluded by the duct and frame edge.

The compressor-room camera preset is partially blocked by the trunk duct filling the upper 40% of frame. The enclosure exterior face is visible but reduced in legibility. Not a scoring defect at the current threshold but the preset framing wastes half the frame on duct geometry the enclosure shot is not meant to evidence.

corrections.instruction: On each compressor package mesh, add three blockout-sufficient elements: (a) a circular grille opening on the top canopy face — a flat disc with a concentric ring or radial-slot cutout, diameter ~0.4 m, sufficient to read as a cooling-fan aperture; (b) a horizontal seam line or extruded band at ~0.85 m height separating the upper canopy from the lower plinth, creating a visible break between the two volumes; (c) a small rectangular panel (0.25 x 0.35 m) on the front face standing slightly proud of the box surface, reading as a control panel. All three can be flat primitives — no surface detail needed at blockout. These three elements are the minimum to cross from 'box' to 'machine' in a still frame.

Add two levels of structural geometry: (a) Column profiles at 8 m bay spacing along both long walls and at all four corners — at blockout a 0.3 x 0.3 m box section or round pipe, 8 m tall, flush with or 0.05 m proud of the cladding plane is sufficient; these must be visible in the open-roof hero view as distinct structural elements, not wall seams. (b) Roof trusses: add at minimum simplified triangular trusses (top chord + bottom chord + one diagonal or vertical per panel) at 8 m bay spacing spanning the 20 m width, at the 8 m eave height; in bay-envelope.png (roof on) the truss underside should be visible as a structural rhythm, not a flat ceiling plane.

Increase the luminaire-grid camera preset elevation to 50-60 degrees (from the current ~20 degrees) so the frame looks substantially downward into the bay. The goal is to show the 6x3 plan grid as a grid — all 18 fixture positions visible in one shot, spacing regularity confirmable by eye. Keep the azimuth to preserve the bay longitudinal read. If the canvas aspect ratio prevents fitting all 18 at high elevation, add a second preset (e.g. 'luminaire-plan') rather than compromising the grid read.
